known_issues.note_20260902_transport_flag_change: The user reported this issue under the id 'dataforseo_import_time_credential_capture' (no such id exists in the file; the closest real id is this one, credential_exposure_in_test_failure_diff, which documents the same import-time credential capture: 'module resolves non-empty login/password that do NOT equal the test literal'). On 2026-09-02 the project-root .env had DATAFORSEO_TRANSPORT_ENABLED set to false (changed from true). This does NOT fix the underlying import-time capture bug (dataforseo_adapter.py still runs load_dotenv() at import and captures DATAFORSEO_TRANSPORT_ENABLED/DATAFORSEO_LOGIN/DATAFORSEO_PASSWORD as module constants, so the armed transport can still resolve real creds from .env), but it DOES remove the immediate live-arming risk because the transport flag itself is now false — the armed transport can no longer fire a real billed call unless the flag is explicitly re-enabled.
known_issues.requires_decision_fix_recommendation: DISTINCT engineering decision from the test-diff symptom above. DataForSEO's credential/arming flags (DATAFORSEO_TRANSPORT_ENABLED, DATAFORSEO_LOGIN, DATAFORSEO_PASSWORD) are captured ONCE at module import via load_dotenv() in dataforseo_adapter.py (lines 96-109), coupling test behavior to CWD/.env state; this is why the armed transport can resolve real creds even when a test sets its own literals. Recommended fix: read these flags LAZILY at call-time via a config getter (e.g., load_config() re-read) instead of pinning them as module-level constants at import, so tests and runtime can control arming deterministically. This is orthogonal to the test-isolation hardening ('empty credential env for tests') and must be preserved as its own decision; not yet voted on or implemented as of 2026-09-02.
